a1-hk-museum-tang-lineage.title: Hong Kong Museum Bulletin, issue 1: the five generations of Emperor Xuanzong

a1-hk-museum-tang-lineage.scopedClaim: Li Kuo/Dezong lived 742-805 and reigned 779-805; his eldest son Li Song/Shunzong lived 761-806 and reigned in 805.

a1-hk-museum-tang-lineage.uncertainty: Year-level dates only. The table gives no location on 25 December 800 and does not by itself date Li Song's designation as crown prince. a1-tang-zhangjing-sun2024.scopedClaim: Zhangjing Temple was a royal Buddhist monastery at Chang'an under Dezong; Dezong received Bodhisattva precepts from Daocheng in 786, and Daocheng resided there from 781 until his death in 803.
a1-tang-zhangjing-sun2024.chronology: Second Zhenyuan year, eighth day of the second month, equated by the author with March 12, 786; Daocheng's residence 781-803.
a1-tang-zhangjing-sun2024.uncertainty: The article supports a specific Buddhist relationship, not exclusive adherence to Buddhism, a single Tang religious establishment or Daocheng's leadership over all Chinese Buddhists. a1-tang-zhangjing-sun2024.license: Reference only; no source prose or images redistributed

a1-aks-aejang.title: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture: Aejang-wang
a1-aks-aejang.locator: Personal data box; Family and personal details; Main activities, paragraphs beginning with accession in June 800 and the regency; concluding paragraph on the killing in July 809.
a1-aks-aejang.scopedClaim: Aejang, originally Kim Cheongmyeong and later renamed Jung-hui, was born in 788, reigned in 800-809, was Soseong and Gyehwa's son and began his reign under the regency of his uncle Kim Eon-seung and grandmother Seongmok.
a1-aks-aejang.uncertainty: The summary says age 12 at accession and the main text age 13, reflecting age conventions that the article does not explain. No conversion of the June/July Korean-calendar months to game days is supplied. Scholars differ on whether the uncle's regency ended in 805 or continued throughout the reign.
a1-aks-aejang.license: Reference only; no source prose or images redistributed

a1-nikh-heondeok.title: Our History Net, Korean History Chronology: Heondeok-wang

a1-nikh-heondeok.scopedClaim: Kim Eon-seung was Soseong's younger brother and Aejang's uncle and regent; he died in 826. The Wonseong-Soseong-Aejang line followed legitimate-descendant succession until his 809 usurpation.
a1-nikh-heondeok.uncertainty: Birth is unknown. The article notes disagreement between Samguk sagi and Samguk yusa about Eon-seung's accomplice in 809; it also describes conflicting records about his wife and children. Those disputed people are not instantiated in this dossier.
a1-nikh-heondeok.license: Reference only; no source prose or images redistributed
